name: Conán

attributes.attribute: cut himself out of the beast
stained red by the serpent's blood

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Conan is the hero of a lake tale, in which a great serpent named Caoranach swallowed him at the water's edge. He cut his own way out, emerging with no skin and no hair. That earned him the name bald Conan, and as the beast died its blood stained the lake red, which is why it is called the Dark Lake. The tale has a Christian version in which Patrick is swallowed and slices free with his crosier.

okr.objective: Conan is the hero who survives the lake serpent and earns a nickname.
key_results: Conan was swallowed by a great serpent.
He cut his way out and lost skin and hair.
The beast's blood stained the lake red.
A later form puts Patrick in the serpent.
